deep.reconstruction:
The page is algebraic scratch work with no title. Its context is unclear; the next page continues with a parameter lambda, quantities a,b,c,a',b',c' and cos(alpha+-alpha') products. Four threads can be reconstructed.

(A) Four bilinear forms in (x,y,z,t) and (x1,y1,z1,t1) whose index pattern is the Klein four-group V4 = Z2^2 acting on {x,y,z,t}:
- F0 = a x x1 + b y y1 + c z z1 + d t t1
- F1 = a1 x y1 + b1 y x1 + c1 z t1 + d1 t z1
- F2 = a2 x z1 + b2 y t1 + c2 z x1 + d2 t y1
- F3 = a3 x t1 + b3 y z1 + c3 z y1 + d3 t x1

As a linear system in (x1,y1,z1,t1), the coefficient matrix has these rows:
- [a x, b y, c z, d t]
- [b1 y, a1 x, d1 t, c1 z]
- [c2 z, d2 t, a2 x, b2 y]
- [d3 t, c3 z, b3 y, a3 x]

The Greek letter in row r sits in column r XOR (letter index). The xyzt terms of the determinant therefore correspond to the complete mappings (orthomorphisms) of Z2^2. There are exactly 8, all giving 3-cycles of the columns, hence all with sign +. Riemann lists exactly these 8 products, in two rows of four:
- a b2 c3 d1, a1 b2 c d3, a2 b c1 d3, a3 b1 c d2
- a b3 c1 d2, a1 b3 c2 d, a2 b1 c3 d, a3 b c2 d1

The second row consists of the inverse 3-cycles of the first. My reading: the coefficient of xyzt in the determinant is their sum.

At the bottom he forms the ratio a b2 c3 d1 / (a2 b c1 d3), i.e. term 1 over term 3 of the first row. He writes it as a product of four double ratios: (a a1/a2 a3)(b2 b3/b b1) * (a a3/a2 a1)(d2 d1/d d3) * (b2 b1/b b3)(c c3/c1 c2) * (d d1/d2 d3)(c2 c3/c c1). This product equals (a b2 c3 d1/(a2 b c1 d3))^2, the square of the ratio.

He also looks for multipliers m, m1, m2, m3 with m b + m1 b1 + m2 b2 + m3 b3 = 0. He then sets m3 = 0 and obtains the linear conditions m(d h + b) = m1(c1 g - b1) and m(c g + a) = m1(d1 h - a1). These are combinations of the forms adapted to the quadrics below. The fragmentary lines (m b + m1 b1) + (m c + m2 c2) g + (m d + m3 d3) h are too incomplete to reconstruct with certainty.

(B) The main computation. The point (x1,y1,z1,t1) is related to (x,y,z,t) by:
- x1 y1 - z1 t1 = xy - zt
- x1 z1 - y1 t1 = h(xz - yt)
- x1 t1 - y1 z1 = g(xt - yz)

These are the three V4-invariant quadrics, scaled by factors 1, h, g. Put P=(xy-zt)^2, Q=(xz-yt)^2, R=(xt-yz)^2, and P1, Q1, R1 likewise for the primed point. Then P1=P, Q1=h^2 Q, R1=g^2 R.

The basic identities are:
- P-Q = (x^2-t^2)(y^2-z^2)
- Q-R = (x^2-y^2)(z^2-t^2)
- R-P = (x^2-z^2)(t^2-y^2)

Their sum gives Riemann's identity (z^2-t^2)(x^2-y^2) + (t^2-x^2)(z^2-y^2) + (x^2-z^2)(t^2-y^2) = 0.

He first squares and subtracts the first two relations: x^2(y^2-h^2 z^2) + t^2(z^2-h^2 y^2) + 2(h^2-1)xyzt = (x1^2-t1^2)(y1^2-z1^2). The cross term xyzt survives here. To remove it on both sides he forms g^2 h^2 [(z^2-t^2)(x^2-y^2) + (t^2-x^2)(z^2-y^2)/g^2 + (x^2-z^2)(t^2-y^2)/h^2] + (z1^2-t1^2)(x1^2-y1^2) + g^2(t1^2-x1^2)(z1^2-y1^2) + h^2(x1^2-z1^2)(t1^2-y1^2) = 0.

This is a correct consequence of the three relations. It is a relation of bidegree (4,4) involving only squares of the coordinates. With A = x^2y^2+z^2t^2, B = x^2z^2+y^2t^2, C = x^2t^2+y^2z^2 (and A1, B1, C1 likewise), he rewrites it as (h^2-g^2)(A-A1) + (g^2-1)(h^2 B - B1) + (1-h^2)(g^2 C - C1) = 0. The three lines (y^2z^2+x^2t^2) g^2(1-h^2) + ..., etc. are exactly these coefficient pairs.

(C) Lower half. He introduces auxiliary parameters a, b, c, d (written as partial-d). He combines (t1^2-x1^2), (t1^2-y1^2), (y1^2-x1^2) with coefficients such as (gb+d)(ga+c), (c-hb)(d-ah), (ga+hb), (a-hd), (gc+a). This seems aimed at writing the quartic relation as a combination of products of differences of squares, i.e. at degenerate members of the family.

A factorization is written: x^2(1-h^2)[h b c + g d(b + h c) + g^2 d^2] = x^2(1-h^2)(g d + b)(g d + h c). The recurring coefficient combination is a(g^2-h^2) + g c(1-h^2) + h(1-g^2) d. This is again the coefficient pattern (h^2-g^2, g^2-1, 1-h^2) of (B), and gh * [((g^2-h^2)/(hg)) b + ((1-g^2)/g) c + ((1-h^2)/h) d] = (g^2-h^2) b + h(1-g^2) c + g(1-h^2) d is the same expression with letters permuted. Expressions like (a+(g/h)b)(a+c/g)(a-hd) - (a+(h/g)b)(a+gc)(a-d/h) are trial elimination steps whose aim I cannot fix with certainty.

Overall: a study of a correspondence/transformation of P^3 preserving the three V4-invariant quadrics up to factors h, g, and of the induced quartic relation in squared coordinates. The setting is reminiscent of theta-function quartic relations and Kummer-type configurations, but the page does not say so.

results.what: Coefficient of xyzt in the determinant of the V4-patterned bilinear system is the sum of 8 products, corresponding to the 8 complete mappings (orthomorphisms) of Z2^2, all with sign +
results.modern_name: Orthomorphisms / transversals of the Klein four-group Latin square; determinant expansion
results.usually_credited_to: Standard combinatorics (orthomorphism notion: Johnson-Dulmage-Mendelsohn 1961, Euler/Latin-square tradition earlier)

results.modern_name: Elementary quadratic identities among V4-invariant quadrics (as in theta-function quartic relations / Kummer configuration)

results.what: Elimination of the cross term xyzt to obtain the relation (h^2-g^2)(A-A1)+(g^2-1)(h^2B-B1)+(1-h^2)(g^2C-C1)=0 for a point pair preserving the three quadrics up to factors 1,h,g
results.modern_name: Quartic correspondence induced by a quadric-preserving transformation of P^3

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but routine algebraic manipulations (quadratic identities, elimination, a determinant expansion) toward an unidentified problem possibly related to theta relations or quadric geometry. Nothing here anticipates a later named result.

Riemann's line x^2(y^2-h^2z^2)+t^2(z^2-h^2y^2)+2(h^2-1)xyzt equals P - h^2 Q = (x1^2-t1^2)(y1^2-z1^2)
The big relation holds given P1=P, Q1=h^2Q, R1=g^2R
The unprimed half rewritten with coefficients h^2-g^2, h^2(g^2-1), g^2(1-h^2) as in Riemann's three lines
Bottom product of double ratios equals the square of the ratio a b2 c3 d1/(a2 b c1 d3)
The 8 listed products are exactly the xyzt-terms of the determinant of the four bilinear forms (all with sign +)
Factorization in the right-middle block holds with g^2 d^2 (fails with g d^2)
